targets.approach: The Rectory is the most striking formation visible from the end of the fire road, and the walk in is over easy terrain. Look for a cairn marking a trail where the approach steepens; there are also many ways to reach the base over bare rock. Going My Way is the obvious crack on the west face, left of the pine tree that Stairway to Heaven passes.
targets.name: Going My Way

targets.approach: The Rectory is the most striking formation visible from the end of the fire road, and the walk in is over easy terrain. Look for a cairn marking a trail where the approach steepens; there are also many ways to reach the base over bare rock. Jacob's Ladder is on the far south end of the west face and climbs through the right side of the Aquinas corner, starting up and right on easy runout ground.
targets.name: Jacob's Ladder

targets.approach: The Rectory is the most striking formation visible from the end of the fire road, and the walk in is over easy terrain. Look for a cairn marking a trail where the approach steepens; there are also many ways to reach the base over bare rock. Stairway to Heaven starts behind a healthy pine tree standing next to the west face.
targets.name: Stairway to Heaven

targets.approach: Talus below the tower scrambles easily to its foot, and the route begins right at the toe.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the line of the route back to the base. From the top, the first rappel goes south, over the ledge below the lower summit, to an anchor on a stance; after that, descend straight down the face. Any anchors you passed with rappel rings on the way up are part of this line.
targets.name: Free Radical

targets.approach: The buttress sits east of the Needles, across the Kern River canyon. Hike the Schaffer Meadow Trail to about Cedar Canyon, then drop down to the wall. The start is in a scooped-out recess of brown blocks and cracks that look solid but questionable.
targets.name: It's No Game
targets.peak: Schaffer Buttress (aka the Wall of Silence)

targets.approach: Turn onto Running Springs School Road, drive to the unmarked gated dirt road on the left, and walk it, then a vague trail, a short way to the base of the crag. It is a west-facing formation above the town of Running Springs. Flake of Flakes is a thin left-facing flake far to the right on the crag, right of Changing Corners.
targets.name: Flake of Flakes

targets.approach: Turn onto Running Springs School Road, drive to the unmarked gated dirt road on the left, and walk it, then a vague trail, a short way to the base of the crag. It is a west-facing formation above the town of Running Springs. Nursery Time lies round the corner to the left of Twin Cracks, on the rock's northwest side; it climbs a flake and then bolted face.
targets.descent_text: Walk off, or rappel from one of the anchors on top of the west face.
targets.name: Nursery Time

targets.approach: Turn onto Running Springs School Road, drive to the unmarked gated dirt road on the left, and walk it, then a vague trail, a short way to the base of the crag. It is a west-facing formation above the town of Running Springs. Primary Grades starts from the ledge a short way left of Flake of Flakes and climbs a right-facing corner system.
targets.name: Primary Grades

targets.approach: Park where Greenway Drive ends at Pioneer Lane, then take trails up the steep rocky hillside past The Gardens toward the Upper Hill blocks. Secret Spot Rock is a big block tucked among trees straight uphill from Shark Fin. Dirty Little Secret is on the left side of its south face.
targets.name: Dirty Little Secret

targets.approach: Leave the Lake George parking area and walk the left-hand shoreline to the lake's far side, where a climbers trail climbs the hillside to the cliff. Continue past the established routes on the north face of the Dike Wall to Sector Mellow, the first slab you reach. Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and right above it, so watch for loose talus and rock. The squeeze crack is the trad line in Sector Evil Seed.
targets.name: Squeeze crack
targets.peak: Sector Mellow and Sector Evil Seed

targets.approach: From the east, begin at the Pine Creek Pass trailhead and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail beyond Upper Pine Lake, branching toward Honeymoon Lake. Carry on through Granite Park to the crest, which you cross at Granite Bear Pass, south of Italy Pass beside Granite Park Spire. Go west cross-country into the Bear Lakes area, passing Big Bear Lake on its north and Little Bear Lake on its south, then trend southwest past tarns to Vee Lake. Walk down its outlet to the East Fork of Bear Creek and work uphill cross-country to the peak. The route is the leftmost gable on the north face.
targets.name: 7th Gable, or Spiral Ridge
targets.parent: Humphreys Basin, Pine Creek & Granite Park

targets.approach: Hike the Robinson Creek Trail beyond Barney Lake toward the junction for Peeler and Robinson Lakes; the small wall is right beside the trail on the left. Hypnocrunch is slightly downhill from one of the switchbacks and is hard to miss. Begin with an undercling off to the right of the crack's line, then move left into it.
targets.name: Hypnocrunch

targets.approach: Approach as for the Mammoth Peak Alcove: on Tioga Road westbound, park at the gravel pull-off a little past the Mono Pass trailhead lot, cross the river, and head through trees to the alcove. From there skirt the base eastward until you reach a prominent buttress cut by cracks, where a mixed line begins at the foot. Flyin' High is left of center on the buttress, just right of Mr. Blue Sky, and climbs bolts to a big diagonal V-shaped slot.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route from the ring anchors.
targets.name: Flyin' High

targets.approach: Approach as for the Mammoth Peak Alcove: on Tioga Road westbound, park at the gravel pull-off a little past the Mono Pass trailhead lot, cross the river, and head through trees to the alcove. From there skirt the base eastward until you reach a prominent buttress cut by cracks, where a mixed line begins at the foot. Mr. Blue Sky is on the left side of the buttress, climbing a lieback crack to a big flake.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the ring anchor at the top, knotting the rope ends.
targets.name: Mr. Blue Sky

targets.approach: From the base of the west face of Parking Lot Rock, follow the trail that wraps around its north side and then heads north; the Slack Wall is a few minutes along. From Two Tree Rock you can instead walk south along its base. The route is at the short, right-hand end of the cove.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor at the top.
targets.name: 2 Cams 2 Bolts Too Old Guys

targets.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Clean Living begins on a vertical crack system about midway between Taphophobia and Fear of Flying, on the gently overhanging orange face.
targets.name: Clean Living

targets.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Delta Crucis is on the southwest face and is one of the westernmost full-length routes, around the corner to the right of The Astraphobia Treatment, and lower on the hillside than the short route that climbs the pillar farther right. It begins in the white groove and aims for the right side of the big headwall.
targets.name: Delta Crucis

targets.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Fear of Fun starts a short way left of The Astraphobia Treatment and joins it higher up.
targets.name: Fear of Fun AKA Southern Comfort

targets.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. This route begins at the foot of an orange pillar, a good way right of the steep part of the main buttress, in a shallow corner that faces right.
targets.descent_text: The climbing turns to a scramble among pines on the arete. Belay in the pines at the sandy spot and walk off to climber's right.
targets.name: FOMO

targets.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Pure Thoughts begins from a belay in the Taphophobia corner and steps right onto flakes on the gently overhanging face.
targets.name: Pure Thoughts

targets.approach: The cliff is the buttress north-northeast of May Lake. From the May Lake trailhead either make a rising traverse across from the lake, or follow the undocumented trail to below the cliffs and then climb straight up to the base. Wet My Pants goes up the deep slot that cuts the middle of the formation straight to the top, beginning at a wide crack above the cluster of trees near the cliff foot.
targets.name: Wet My Pants, AKA Southern Fried

targets.approach: Drive forest road 2N13 and then 2N13D to their junction and park; a climbers trail goes up the ramp above the gully, and a steep bushy scramble leads on to the pinnacle's southwest side. Crack 1742 is a short crack just round the corner, right of Napoleon Syndrome.
targets.name: Crack 1742

targets.approach: Drive forest road 2N13 and then 2N13D to their junction and park; a climbers trail goes up the ramp above the gully, and a steep bushy scramble leads on to the pinnacle's southwest side. Mama's Crack is the obvious crack and corner line on the lower southwest face, with a bulge to pull near the top.
targets.name: Mama's Crack

targets.approach: Drive forest road 2N13 and then 2N13D to their junction and park; a climbers trail goes up the ramp above the gully, and a steep bushy scramble leads on to the pinnacle's southwest side. Papa's Crack is the roofy hand crack to the left of Mama's Crack.
targets.name: Papa's Crack

targets.approach: Pull off on the outer edge of Tioga Road right under the formation and climb the shattered slabs above the road to the base, or start from the Warren Creek trailhead at the unofficial campground on the bend in US 120. The line follows the east ridge, which can be joined at the saddle reached from the back side, or traversed in full from Warren Creek, a loose option.
targets.name: Northeast Ridge

targets.approach: Take the McGee Creek trail up McGee Creek Canyon, and before the side trail east to Steelhead Lake, fork right onto the old mining road into Baldwin Canyon. Follow it until the pillar comes into view on the left. The route is the clear crack splitting the middle of the pillar.
targets.name: A. Splitter

targets.approach: The wall is reached either from Mineral King via Monarch Lake and over Glacier Pass, or by crossing Timber Gap and following Cliff Creek up to Spring Lake. The wall rises directly above the lake near the head of Cliff Creek Canyon and is split into three buttresses. Climb the talus to the wall's lowest point, where a square-cut corner system facing right rises off the ground. Friends climbs the face and cracks just to its right, just left of the other established routes.
targets.descent_text: Either rappel the line using the fixed anchors, starting from the top of the last roped pitch, or walk off from the summit.
targets.name: Friends

targets.approach: Park at St. Marys Pass and hike to the top, then head north toward Stanislaus Peak. The top of the crag is a long way out, and a safe line down to the base can be hard to find. The route is the pillar standing in the gully's midline, close to where a party would rappel in.
targets.name: Echo location

targets.approach: From the Mosquito Flat trailhead, follow the Little Lakes Valley Trail beyond Chickenfoot Lake. A little past the lake, before the turnoff for Morgan Pass, the trail crosses the creek on stepping stones, and the crag is right beside the crossing. Daisies Dihedral is the largest dihedral on the wall.
targets.name: Daisies Dihedral

targets.approach: From the Mosquito Flat trailhead, follow the Little Lakes Valley Trail beyond Chickenfoot Lake. A little past the lake, before the turnoff for Morgan Pass, the trail crosses the creek on stepping stones, and the crag is right beside the crossing. Stepping Stone Crack is the clear full-height crack on the main face, immediately left of the biggest dihedral.
targets.name: Stepping Stone Crack

targets.approach: Follow the approach to Indian Buttress, then continue up into Echo Gully; the Wall of Echos is the big steep cliff band on the immediate left. A climbers trail runs along its base if you stay to the extreme left just after the Little Indian. Land Animal climbs a crack that starts uphill of Swooped, running up to a small roof.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route. From the ledge with the anchor shared with Rain Shadow, it is easier to rappel Rain Shadow than to continue down Land Animal.
targets.name: Land Animal

targets.approach: Follow the approach to Indian Buttress, then continue up into Echo Gully; the Wall of Echos is the big steep cliff band on the immediate left. A climbers trail runs along its base if you stay to the extreme left just after the Little Indian. Rain Shadow starts in a wide gully uphill from Land Animal and finishes in a dihedral.
targets.name: Rain Shadow

targets.approach: Hike up to the south face of the Rectory and go east, then find a way across; the line goes high past the Rectory south face and up second-class ground toward the Rectory east face, then past the Convent and Mosque notch. Direct routes through oak and mahogany are possible but thick. The route tracks a steep water streak toward the right side of the Synagogue's west face, and begins with an unprotected easy slab to a ledge.
targets.name: Judgement Day

targets.approach: Park where Greenway Drive ends at Pioneer Lane, then take trails up the steep rocky hillside past The Gardens toward the Upper Hill blocks. Table Top Rock is a small block uphill and west of Secret Spot Rock. Pinch It and Leave It is on the right side of the south face, starting off a boulder to a prominent flake.
targets.name: Pinch It and Leave It

targets.approach: Park where Greenway Drive ends at Pioneer Lane, then take trails up the steep rocky hillside past The Gardens toward the Upper Hill blocks. Taggers is a large, low-angle formation a short way east of Cockell's Dome, directly downhill and south of Lime-Aid. ASCA is on its southwest face.
targets.name: ASCA

targets.approach: Park in the northwest-facing turnout on the north side of the road east of Holcomb Valley Campground; the south-facing granite slab is visible from the road a short walk north. Canon is the offwidth just right of Enterprise.
targets.name: Canon

targets.approach: Park in the northwest-facing turnout on the north side of the road east of Holcomb Valley Campground; the south-facing granite slab is visible from the road a short walk north. Fine Point is the finger crack right of the Canon offwidth.
targets.name: Fine Point

targets.approach: Park at the hairpin turn and follow the Coven trail north across the first ridge and the seasonal stream bed on the way up to the Dragonlance and Voodoo walls. About midway up the gully you reach the Addams Family slab on your left. Pugsley is the crack on the right side of the slab.
targets.descent_text: Walk off by scrambling down the left (west) side of the slab.
targets.name: Pugsley

targets.approach: Park where Greenway Drive ends at Pioneer Lane, then take trails up the steep rocky hillside past The Gardens toward the Upper Hill blocks. The Egg is a large rounded block with a downed tree at its base, uphill and a little northwest of Lime-Aid. Split Open and Melt is on the left side of the north face and starts off a rock at the base.
targets.name: Split Open and Melt
